profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record sits at 7300 World Communications Drive in Omaha, Nebraska, one of two nearly identical building footprints roughly 65 to 75 meters apart at the same address. Both were originally tagged by an OpenStreetMap contributor in 2019 with the label MCI, a name tied to MCI Communications and later MCI Inc, the long-distance and data-networking carrier that Verizon Communications acquired in January 2006 for roughly 8.5 billion dollars. MCI Inc was folded into what became Verizon Business, the enterprise and wholesale arm of Verizon that inherited MCI former fiber routes, switching centers, and network-operations real estate around the country. In October 2023, a different contributor relabeled both Omaha buildings from MCI to Verizon and added a telecom=data_center tag, based on the edit history, that relabeling appears to have relied on aerial-imagery interpretation rather than a site visit, business filing, or press source. That leaves a plausible but unconfirmed chain of inference: this could well be a legacy MCI-era long-haul network facility that Verizon now operates as part of its wholesale and enterprise network, functioning as a switching or transport hub rather than a commercial colocation data center of the kind featured elsewhere on this site. Omaha World Communications Drive is a known concentration point for carrier and telecom infrastructure in eastern Nebraska given the city long-standing role as a hub for telecommunications and financial-services back-office operations, which is consistent with a network facility being sited there. No operator-published fact sheet, SEC filing, county property record, or trade-press article naming this specific address as a Verizon or MCI facility could be located this session. Nebraska is also outside the nine-state footprint (Connecticut through Virginia and the District of Columbia) where Verizon operates as the legacy incumbent local exchange carrier from its Bell Atlantic and NYNEX heritage, so this is very unlikely to be an old regional Bell central office. Readers should treat the Verizon and MCI names on this record as genuine but the facility function as unconfirmed pending a primary source. Nothing about capacity, technical space, tier rating, or year built is asserted here because no source establishes those figures for this specific building.

reading.body:
This Omaha facility is a Verizon network switching and data center on World Communications Drive, a street purpose-built for this campus. No power capacity is published for the site. Verizon operates this as an internal network facility rather than a customer-facing colocation venue, which means its AI hosting role depends on internal allocation decisions that are not transparent to external observers.

Nebraska has no published power capacity data from any data center operator in this registry. This facility ranks first by published megawatts in the state only because the state publishes no figures at all. Twenty-one facilities are mapped in Nebraska statewide, and this is one of two Verizon buildings in Omaha sitting roughly 90 meters apart, likely the same campus or adjacent structures.

Without published power specifications, no calculation of rack or accelerator density is possible. The inability to measure this facility's actual IT load means its significance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from public information. Whether it matters to AI deployment will depend entirely on how much internal Verizon demand Omaha can absorb, a number the operator has not disclosed.
